To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) global health is taught in 45.5% of required didactic courses, 2) 57.7% of PharmD programs offer global health elective courses, 3) 78.8% of programs offer introductory and/or advanced experiential learning opportunities in global health, 4) 65.4% of PharmD schools offer medical mission trips, and 5) 45.1% of PharmD students have completed a global health elective.

28/55 (50.9%) US PharmD programs offered global health coursework, 41/52 (78.8% of those who provided information) offered global health experiential education and 34/52 (65.4% of those who offered global health experients) offered global health medical missions.
43% of the 127 US doctor of pharmacy programs surveyed offer some form of global health education, and the majority of these programs provide global health education through experiential education.
